channel.title: Pier & Point · Mission Bay South Block 9A
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Mission Bay South Block 9A (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Mission Bay South Block 9A: The October 20, 2023 city memo asks for an additional…
item.description: The October 20, 2023 city memo asks for an additional $8,000,000 in gap funding, which would bring the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure's (OCII) total investment to $83,184,522; the sources read do not show when or whether the request was approved, although the developer's 2025 press release gives about $83 million from OCII. The ribbon-cutting is now dated September 26, 2025, the day of the Mayor's release. The general contractor is named in city documents as Nibbi, Nibbi Construction/Baines and a Baines-Nibbi joint venture. SF YIMBY reports solar panels, not specifically rooftop panels. Source: https://media.api.sf.gov/documents/Approved_400_China_Basin_Additional_Gap_Funding_-_LC_10-20-23.pdf; https://www.sf.gov/news-mayor-lurie-cuts-ribbon-on-148-new-affordable-homes-for-first-time-homeowners-in-mission-bay.

item.title: Correction · Mission Bay South Block 9A: 400 China Basin no longer shows a construction-start…
item.description: 400 China Basin no longer shows a construction-start date: OCII's October 2023 memo says construction began in July 2022, while SF YIMBY (October 2025) says it started in 2023. The summary also no longer gives one building area; sources differ. Source: OCII Loan Committee memo, 2023-10-20 (media.api.sf.gov/documents/Approved_400_China_Basin_Additional_Gap_Funding_-_LC_10-20-23.pdf); SF YIMBY, 2025-10-02.
item.source: OCII Loan Committee memo, 2023-10-20 (media.api.sf.gov/documents/Approved_400_China_Basin_Additional_Gap_Funding_-_LC_10-20-23.pdf); SF YIMBY, 2025-10-02

item.title: Correction · Mission Bay South Block 9A: The record dated the ribbon-cutting to October 2, 2025…
item.description: The record dated the ribbon-cutting to October 2, 2025, which is the SF YIMBY article's publication date; the article says the ceremony was held 'last week', and the project's press release (dated August 21, 2025) announced a celebration for September 26. The record now says late September 2025. A milestone that put the start of construction in February 2023 cited only a website's home page; OCII's October 2023 memo says construction began in July 2022, which the record already carried, so the February 2023 entry was removed. Also corrected: the press release's date (August 21, not the event date), the GreenPoint Platinum claim (now attributed to the project's press release) and the unsupported 'raised ground floor' detail (removed), the contractor no longer called a joint venture, the architect's 165,000 sq ft figure (removed), and the July 22, 2019 proposal date now reads as the submission deadline. Source: SF YIMBY, 2025-10-02 (https://sfyimby.com/2025/10/ribbon-cutting-held-for-affordable-units-at-400-china-basin-street-in-san-francisco.html); 400 China Basin press release, 2025-08-21 (https://www.400chinabasin.com/press-media/press-release); SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development, Loan Committee memo, 2023-10-20 (https://media.api.sf.gov/documents/Approved_400_China_Basin_Additional_Gap_Funding_-_LC_10-20-23.pdf).
item.source: SF YIMBY, 2025-10-02 (https://sfyimby.com/2025/10/ribbon-cutting-held-for-affordable-units-at-400-china-basin-street-in-san-francisco.html); 400 China Basin press release, 2025-08-21 (https://www.400chinabasin.com/press-media/press-release); SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development, Loan Committee memo, 2023-10-20 (https://media.api.sf.gov/documents/Approved_400_China_Basin_Additional_Gap_Funding_-_LC_10-20-23.pdf)

item.title: Under construction · Mission Bay South Block 9A: OCII staff memo (dated this day)… (Oct 20, 2023)
item.description: OCII staff memo (dated this day) asks the Citywide Affordable Housing Loan Committee for an additional $8,000,000 in gap funding, which would bring total OCII investment to $83,184,522, to offset rising mortgage rates' effect on affordability; no approval date is shown in the sources read (Oct 20, 2023). Source: San Francisco Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development / OCII (primary city agency document), 2023-10-20.
item.source: San Francisco Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development / OCII (primary city agency document), 2023-10-20
